subject: Phased regional recovery SLA proposal and temporary RPO/RTO carveout
messages:
From: Sara Bennett <sara.bennett@orion-pay.com>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Cc: contracts@orion-pay.com, dave.lin@orion-pay.com
Date: Mon, 1 Apr 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: phased EU failover SLA w/ cost trade-off

Rishi,

Thanks for the productive demo last week. We reviewed Redwood's multi-region options internally and have a follow-up asks from ops and finance: Orion needs an EU failover commitment, but the run-rate cost of fully warm active-active is not in budget for the first 12 months.

High level ask: can Redwood offer a phased recovery SLA that guarantees a defined RTO/RPO for critical payment flows in the EU while allowing a relaxed RTO for non-critical flows? Specifically:
- Critical payment API: target RTO 15 minutes / RPO 1 minute during declared failover window
- Non-critical analytics and batch: acceptable RTO up to 6 hours / RPO up to 2 hours

We understand this is non-standard. We'd be open to a time-limited exception (12 months) with a measurable performance credit schedule tied to the critical-API RTO. Attached: our expected traffic mix and an ops runbook describing what we consider critical.

Can you confirm feasibility and a ballpark on the cost delta vs your standard multi-region SLA?

Thanks,
Sara Bennett
Head of Infrastructure
Orion Payments

Attachments: orion-demand-plan.xlsx (spreadsheet)
From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
To: Sara Bennett <sara.bennett@orion-pay.com>
Cc: naomi_feldman@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 2 Apr 2029 11:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: phased EU failover SLA w/ cost trade-off

Sara —

Appreciate the detail and attachment. Short answer: yes, we can propose a phased/regional recovery SLA, but it requires a few guardrails and an exception in our standard contract for the first 12 months.

A few notes from engineering and product (summary):
- We can partition traffic by route/model so critical payment API traffic is pinned to a *hot* warm-standby pool in the EU with pre-warmed reserved capacity. That pool would provide sub-20s latency under failover and allow an effective RTO ~15 minutes with KV prefix caching and active replication.
- Non-critical traffic can be routed to our burst/cold pool with slower startup ramps; that supports the longer RTO you outlined.
- RPO guarantees for the critical route rely on cross-region async replication with frequent checkpoints; 1 minute RPO is aggressive but achievable with tuned replication and write-ahead buffering. There is a modest risk window during switchover where a small fraction of in-flight tokens could be lost; this is what the contract carveout would need to capture.

Commercially, the cost delta vs our standard multi-region SLA is primarily driven by reserved capacity for the hot pool + higher network egress for aggressive replication. Ballpark: +30–45% for the first 12 months depending on peak concurrency. We can quantify after we see the demand spreadsheet (thanks for sending).

I'll loop in Naomi on specific credit/penalty language and Marissa for the support playbook and runbook alignment. If you're happy, we'll draft a temporary addendum that lays out RTO/RPO by route, credit schedule, and acceptance test steps.

Next step: Naomi, can you sketch the technical acceptance tests and a proposed credit ladder (e.g., % credit for missed RTO windows at critical API)?

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Sales Engineering | Redwood Inference
From: naomi_feldman@redwood.com
To: Sara Bennett <sara.bennett@orion-pay.com>, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 3 Apr 2029 08:46:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: phased EU failover SLA w/ cost trade-off

Sara / team —

Thanks — based on the spreadsheet I ran a few scenarios. Outlines below are intended to be included in the addendum PDF (attached). I kept the language operational so Legal can adapt.

Proposed technical requirements (critical route):
- Warm pool sizing: reserved GPUs N = 0.15 * peak concurrent inference tokens (rounded up) with an autoscale buffer of 20% during declared failover windows.
- Replication cadence: async checkpoint every 30s, continuous write-ahead log with per-request ACKs to the primary. Secondary applies replay with max lag target 60s.
- Failover orchestration: automated switchover with health gating; manual rollback option if data drift > configured threshold.
- Acceptance test: two-step validation — (1) synthetic traffic spike simulating 10% of peak for 15 minutes with <20s cold-start latency on failover; (2) end-to-end payment success rate >= 99.9% over a 1-hour soak post-switch.

Credit ladder (example):
- If critical API RTO > 15m but <= 30m during declared failover: 10% monthly service credit on Redwood usage for that month (capped at 50% for repeat occurrences).
- If RTO > 30m: 25% monthly service credit + joint incident review and mandatory corrective plan.
- RPO miss (data loss > 1m): 15% credit and root cause report; repeat occurrences escalate credits cumulatively.

Notes on exceptions: 12-month trial period; after 12 months Redwood reserves the right to rebaseline pricing and capacity allocation. Also propose a SLO review milestone at month 6 to validate the traffic model and adjust sizes.

Attached: redwood-phased-recovery-proposal.pdf (draft addendum), diagram-phased-warm-standby.png

—Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Director, Reliability Engineering | Redwood Inference
From: Sara Bennett <sara.bennett@orion-pay.com>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Cc: contracts@orion-pay.com, dave.lin@orion-pay.com, naomi_feldman@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 4 Apr 2029 10:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: phased EU failover SLA w/ cost trade-off

Rishi / Naomi —

This looks like the right level of detail. A few clarifying asks from our side before we route to Legal:
1) Can the acceptance test be run in a non-declarative maintenance window (i.e., we want to confirm failover without a live incident and without impacting customers)?
2) Please confirm how billing credits are calculated (based on the Redwood usage invoice line for the impacted month?) and whether credits are refundable against prior invoices or only future usage.
3) We need a defined termination trigger: if after six months our traffic shape materially exceeds the model (we'll provide telemetry), we want an option to convert to full active-active or renegotiate without penalty.

If you can confirm those three items we will share the draft with our contracts team and propose minor redlines.

Thanks,
Sara
From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: Contracts Team <contracts@orion-pay.com>, Sara Bennett <sara.bennett@orion-pay.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, naomi_feldman@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 5 Apr 2029 09:31:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: phased EU failover SLA w/ cost trade-off (legal review)

Sara / Orion contracts —

Thanks for sending. A few commercial/legal clarifications from our side and proposed redline points:
- Acceptance test: Redwood will perform the acceptance tests in a planned, mutually agreed maintenance window. We will run validation on a mirrored environment and a staged failover with synthetic traffic to avoid customer impact. We'll include an ops checklist that documents steps and rollback criteria.
- Credits: credits are applied as a percentage credit to Redwood's invoice for the affected month; credits will be issued against future invoices unless otherwise agreed in writing.
- Termination/Conversion trigger: we are open to a mid-term conversion clause (month 6) where either party can request rebaseline. If Orion wants to convert to active-active, Redwood will provide a commercial proposal and reasonable lead time to provision.

I'll prepare a marked-up addendum with the three points integrated, plus a short joint operational schedule template and sign-off form. Expect the redline by EOD.

—Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference
From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
To: Sara Bennett <sara.bennett@orion-pay.com>, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: naomi_feldman@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 5 Apr 2029 17:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: phased EU failover SLA w/ cost trade-off (next steps)

Sara —

Thanks for the quick turnaround. To summarize next steps and timelines: 
1) Kimberly to circulate the redlined addendum (today).
2) Orion contracts to review and return redlines (target: Tue, Apr 9).
3) On agreement, Redwood will schedule a readiness test in a mutually agreed maintenance window within 10 business days of signature.
4) Naomi and Marissa will create an acceptance-test runbook and a 6-month SLO review plan; we'll share telemetry dashboard access.

I'll attach the current draft addendum and an ops checklist to the signed copy once we have redlines. Appreciate the collaborative approach — aiming to keep Orion in a protected posture while balancing cost realities.

Regards,
Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Sales Engineering | Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-phased-recovery-proposal.pdf (updated draft), diagram-phased-warm-standby.png
